Today you’ll visit the ceremonial site of Orongo.




First, climb the slopes of the Rano Kau volcano to a viewpoint on the rim of its vast crater. Below, a lake is surrounded by distinctive vegetation.




Continue to the ceremonial village of Orongo, where the island’s leader was traditionally chosen through a risky competition. In spring, clan representatives gathered in the stone houses and waited for the sacred manutara bird to appear so they could determine who would become Tangata Manu, the Birdman.
Row of stone moai on Easter Island under a cloudy sky, Chile
Moai statues on a stone platform on Easter Island, Chile

The tour begins on the island’s south coast. You’ll see the unrestored platforms of Ahu Vaihu in Hanga Te‘e Bay and Akahanga, where King Hotu Matu‘a is thought to be buried.




Continue to Rano Raraku, where most of the moai were carved. There are about 900 stone statues, of which 397 are still lying or standing on the slopes of the extinct volcano. Here you can see especially clearly how the giant figures were carved and moved.




After a boxed lunch, visit Ahu Tongariki, the island’s largest platform, with 15 restored moai. Continue to Ahu Te Pito Kura and the site known as the ‘Navel of the World’.




The final stop is Anakena Beach, with warm turquoise water, white sand, palm trees and the Ahu Nau Nau platform. There’s time to walk and swim.




Return to Hanga Roa, transfer to the airport, fly to Santiago and transfer on arrival.
